claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children do you have that you'd like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child, my son Alex. He's 18 now and lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can still claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can see you have one child, Alex, who is 18 years old and lives with you.

Before I can assess his eligibility, I need to understand the rules better. Let me check the specific criteria for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that context. Based on what you've told me, I can see that Alex is 18 years old. According to the Child Benefit rules I've just reviewed, there's an important age threshold to consider.

**To help me determine Alex's eligibility, I need to know: Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as university, college, sixth form, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not studying at the moment. He finished school and he's just been at home for now, trying to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex is 18, has finished school, and is not currently in approved education or training.

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with a clear answer about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

According to the government rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child **under 16**. However, there is an exception: you can continue to claim Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over **if they stay in approved education or training**.

Since Alex is 18 and is not currently in approved education or training, he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: Child Benefit is normally available for children under 16. For children aged 16 or over, the rules allow you to continue claiming only if they're in approved education or training (such as university, college, sixth form, or an apprenticeship). Since Alex is 18 and not currently in any approved education or training, he falls outside the eligibility criteria.

If Alex does decide to pursue education or training in the future, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again during that period. If you have any questions or your circumstances change, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for further advice.
